The final answer of 84 is incorrect. The proposed solution never derives it: it states "it is found that ∠APC = 84°" without computation. The "equilateral triangle" reinterpretation is also unjustified, since the angles 20°, 46° and 26° do not sum to 360°.

I checked the answer numerically. Place A at the origin with AB = AC = 1, B at angle 0° and C at angle 92°. Then P = u(cos 20°, sin 20°) and Q = v(cos 66°, sin 66°). Requiring BP = PQ = QC gives u ≈ 0.582 and v ≈ 0.669, with common length ≈ 0.495.

Then:
- P ≈ (0.547, 0.199) and C ≈ (−0.035, 0.999).
- PA = (−0.547, −0.199) and PC = (−0.582, 0.800).
- cos∠APC ≈ 0.1587 / (0.5818 × 0.9894) ≈ 0.276, so ∠APC ≈ 74°.

This does not match 84°.

VERDICT: REJECT
